Interpretation and Intention

Umberto Eco distinguishes among intention of the author, text, and reader. This triad remains powerful for analyzing ambiguity and interpretive limits.

For AI-mediated communication, an additional layer can be proposed: intentio algorithmi. This names the operational tendency of algorithmic systems—the patterns encouraged by objectives, training data, and ranking logic—even when no human author directly intended a specific output.

Use this page to test where classical intent frameworks hold and where algorithmic mediation requires new vocabulary.
